Built a definitive line-by-line skeleton for all 56 vilna lines before writing any English, re-extracting the raw Hebrew fresh from the packet, cross-checked where relevant against a citation to Yoma 32b (self-reference, 'Amar Lahem HaMemuneh'). Content covers: the ideal order of the day's service if everything were stated sequentially, and why it is not (l01, l02, l04, vilna 1-4); Rabbi Zeira's challenge that the external goat interrupts the sequence, and Abaye's answer that the first 'exit' verse governs the rams (l06, l07, vilna 4-13); Rava's own proof from 'that he already wore' that a second vestment change intervenes (l09, vilna 14-18); the extended objection that the Mishnah's own order (that the HP does not see the burnt bull and goat, since it happens while he still wears white) apparently contradicts the stated sequence, and its resolution that all agree the sin-offering fats come at the third immersion regardless (l15, l19, l20a, vilna 19-29); the long meikara/hashta exchange over whether 'the one who sends' and 'the one who burns' each refer to the original dispatch/burning or to the present verse's own placement, resolved by Rava's alternative proof that the goat 'shall stand alive' only until the time of atonement (l20b, l21, l22, vilna 30-50); the sender's return to report to the High Priest the next day, with the folk blessing exchanged among the sages of Pumbedita (l24, l25, vilna 50-52); and the extended aggadic close on marketplaces, life's reversals, and the wordplay identifying Torah scholars as 'ishim' rather than 'anashim' (l27, l28, l30, vilna 52-55).

Ten raw lines are genuine dibbur-boundary straddles, the densest being vilnaLine 46 (l20b/l21, the meikara-to-hashta pivot) and several two-clause bridges elsewhere (vilnaLine 3, 4, 17, 26, 28, 50, 52, 53, 54).
